instructions: People pay attention in two ways. In the sensing mode, you take in what is here through your senses (sounds, textures, light, your breath) without needing to do anything with it. In the doing mode, you use what you know to plan, solve, judge, fix or get something done. Both are useful. These questions ask how you move between them. How much do you agree with each statement? There are no right or wrong answers.

items.text: I recognize that the sensing mode is always available to me
I can put a simple word to what I am sensing without getting caught up in thinking about it
I can notice whether something feels pleasant, unpleasant or neutral before I react to it
I can see clearly how easily the doing mode can become my default
I understand that stress and threat naturally pull people toward familiar habits and the doing mode
I am more able to move into the sensing mode when I feel safe and secure
I feel confident in my ability to move into the sensing mode
I see myself as having two gears that I can choose between: sensing and doing
Even when I am stressed, I try to make space for the sensing mode
I welcome surprise when I am in the sensing mode, rather than trying to predict or control what happens
Time in the sensing mode leaves me with a sense of awe or wonder
For me, the sensing mode feels different in kind from the doing mode of planning, fixing, and achieving
What I notice in the moment feels complete on its own, without needing to add meaning to it
I notice quickly when I have drifted into autopilot without meaning to
I do not view it as a personal failing when stress narrows my attention. I recognize it as a natural response
I notice that feeling unsafe or threatened makes it harder for me to stay open to my senses
I can move into the sensing mode even in the middle of a stressful or demanding moment
I realize I always have a choice between the sensing mode and the doing mode
I place extra value on returning to the sensing mode in moments when stress is pulling me toward narrow, familiar responses
I value being free from the need to have control or know what comes next
Engaging my senses fully opens up new ideas or perspectives I would not have noticed otherwise
I can let a sensation simply be, without figuring out what it means or where it leads
I can tell the difference between a moment that calls for the doing mode and one that calls for the sensing mode
I can sense when my surroundings feel safe enough to explore openly
Once I notice I have slipped into the doing mode without meaning to, I know how to shift back
I place real value on time spent in the sensing mode, not only on getting things done
I enjoy the process of discovering something new, not just the outcome of what I find
I look forward to the feeling that comes from sensory exploration, not just the skill of doing it
I notice when I keep doing something out of habit after it has stopped helping
I can move into the sensing mode in unfamiliar or new settings, not just when I set time aside to practise
Returning to the sensing mode feels worth prioritizing, even when I am busy
Seeing something from a new or unexpected perspective feels valuable to me in its own right
Moving into the sensing mode comes easily to me in everyday life
I am drawn to uncertainty and ambiguity, not just tolerant of it, when I am in the sensing mode
